topic: Sharp sign-ratio closure and singularity-robust inference for multi-setting OVB bounds. Audit Huntington-Klein 2026 and released hetset 0.1.0: replace the bias-difference LP by the sharp componentwise union P+ or P- implied by positive bounded bias ratios; prove converse attainability, log-cycle/Farkas certificates, exact branch-LP or MILP computation, an unconditional support relaxation gap, and exact requested-pin gaps. Construct feasible confidence sets uniformly valid at zero bias, branch/basis ties, and n^(-1/2)-weak supershort ratio denominators using numerical-delta inference off singularities and undivided primitive-moment inversion near them, with pointwise oracle recovery in regular regions. Reimplement R/Python/Stata routines and reanalyse ACS returns-to-college pinning. Do not stop at the counterexample, routine sign enumeration, or generic projection inference.

open_problems.open_problem: Characterize the sharp identified set under positive bounded cross-setting OVB ratios as the affine image of the componentwise union P+ or P-, prove converse attainability, and determine exactly when Huntington-Klein's bias-difference polytope is a strict outer relaxation.

source_refs.claim: Assumption 3 imposes positive bounded ratios and hence common signs, but Proposition 4 proves only containment in a polytope assembled from pairwise bias-difference bounds.
source_refs.author: Nick Huntington-Klein

source_refs.excerpt: the single branch-free exact-mass partial-transport polytope is the exact projection of compatible laws
lem:conditional-trimming-fiber-attainment + lem:latent-completion-pasting — the sharp ⊇ attainment construction
prove an open-set separation between the rectangular ... interval and the true common-structural-error sharp set

open_problems.why_unsolved: Huntington-Klein replaces the shared equations B_j = rho_jk B_k by separately extremized difference intervals, discarding both the common sign and global multiplicative compatibility of one bias vector; Proposition 4 establishes containment, not a converse. The prior catalogue shows that an observable polytope becomes sharp only after an endpoint-preserving compatible-law construction, and flags open-set separation from rectangular relaxations as the publishable strengthening. Here the first missing proof step is an explicit omitted-variable/regression completion realizing every point of P+ or P-; a lone counterexample cannot establish the requested unconditional support relaxation gap.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An if-and-only-if identification theorem equating the effect set to the affine image of P+ union P-, a constructive observationally equivalent OVB completion for every feasible point, and support-function equality conditions or a symbolic open-cell witness on which the bias-difference LP endpoint lies strictly outside the sharp union.

writing_exemplar.why: Its multi-setting motivation, proportional-confounding formulation, and returns-to-college application are the direct narrative to retain while correcting the identification boundary.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Quasi-experimental variation is not portable across settings -> separate sensitivity bounds ignore dependence in OVB -> positive ratio restrictions sharpen the joint effect set -> the sharp sign-union closure must replace a merely containing difference polytope

method_exemplars.technique: Derive LP bounds over latent feasible objects and prove sharpness by constructing a latent distribution attaining every feasible extreme.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The OVB result likewise needs both an optimization characterization and a converse showing that every point in the proposed set is generated by admissible latent confounding.

method_exemplars.technique: Express compatibility as finite-dimensional polyhedral-cone membership and use equivalent primal and dual descriptions.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Each fixed-sign ratio-restricted bias component is a polyhedral cone intersected with primitive bounds, so cone membership and separation are structurally analogous.

method_exemplars.technique: Calibrate projection intervals by repeatedly solving relaxed feasibility programs and prove uniform asymptotic coverage for projected partially identified parameters.
method_exemplars.why_closest: After sharpness, setting-specific and pinned OVB bounds are projections of a finite inequality-defined causal parameter set.

open_problems.open_problem: Construct confidence sets for sharp multi-setting OVB bounds that are uniformly valid at zero bias, sign-branch or LP-basis ties, and n^(-1/2)-weak supershort denominators, while recovering numerical-delta oracle inference on regular submodels.

source_refs.claim: The paper treats its bounds as population objects, names multi-setting inference as future work, and warns that supershort ratio calibration is unstable near a zero denominator.
source_refs.author: Nick Huntington-Klein

source_refs.claim: For directionally but not fully differentiable maps, the ordinary bootstrap is generally inconsistent under Gaussian limits and derivative-aware resampling is required.
source_refs.author: Zheng Fang and Andres Santos

source_refs.claim: The numerical delta method consistently handles directionally differentiable maps and is uniformly valid for specified convex Lipschitz classes.
source_refs.author: Han Hong and Jessie Li

source_refs.claim: For multiple parameter ratios, Wald methods fail near denominator discontinuities while joint-test inversion yields Fieller-type identification-robust regions.
source_refs.author: Denis Bolduc, Lynda Khalaf, and Clement Yelou

source_refs.claim: Near locally unidentified transformations, valid confidence sets for unbounded parameters must be unbounded with positive probability, ruling out uniformly valid always-bounded Wald sets.
source_refs.author: Jean-Marie Dufour

source_refs.claim: Conditional test inversion attains uniformly correct asymptotic size without identification assumptions and retains efficiency in strongly identified Gaussian moment models.
source_refs.author: Isaiah Andrews and Anna Mikusheva

source_refs.excerpt: does not claim that the proposed cross-fitted numerical directional-delta confidence region has uniform coverage
Uniform coverage with simultaneous cut ties, near-active faces, and changing survivor support is explicitly open
zero first stages, tangencies, shrinking gaps, exchange ties, singleton or zero-width sets ... are excluded
state a corrected resampling or contact-set estimator with a theorem not implied by Fang-Santos

open_problems.why_unsolved: Away from zero denominators, a sharp endpoint is still a max or min over sign branches and LP bases, so ties leave only directional differentiability and invalidate a naive bootstrap. At an exact or n^(-1/2)-local supershort denominator, the ratio and sign maps themselves are discontinuous; Dufour's impossibility result prevents uniformly valid always-bounded Wald output. The prior runs separately leave numerical-delta uniformity at ties, changing active faces, and weak-denominator boundary cases open. The missing step is one joint confidence event for undivided coefficient-change, short-regression, and bias-bound moments whose inversion covers both sign branches near the singular zone, coupled to a proof that a data-dependent transition to numerical-delta inference does not lose uniform coverage.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A feasible primitive-moment test-inversion confidence set with triangular-array uniform coverage over exact-zero and n^(-1/2)-weak denominator sequences and all branch/basis ties, together with an explicit numerical directional derivative off singularities and a pointwise theorem equating the hybrid set to the unique-active-branch oracle procedure on separated regular submodels.

writing_exemplar.why: It introduces supershort calibration, states the near-zero denominator pathology, and supplies the ACS application in which identification-robust inference matters.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Observed control-induced coefficient changes calibrate relative hidden bias -> calibration requires ratios and estimated signs -> small changes make those transforms weakly identified while branch endpoints remain nonsmooth -> inference must invert undivided moments near zero and recover sharper numerical-delta inference away from zero

method_exemplars.technique: Estimate the directional derivative by finite perturbations of the full endpoint optimization map and bootstrap the resulting numerical derivative.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Sharp OVB endpoints are nonsmooth value functions of asymptotically normal primitive moments whenever branches or LP bases tie.

method_exemplars.technique: Derive the Hadamard directional derivative, diagnose ordinary-bootstrap inconsistency, and resample through a consistent derivative estimator.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Branch and basis ties are precisely points of directional rather than full differentiability, so the corrected resampling proof is the relevant regular-zone template.

method_exemplars.technique: Invert a joint test on numerator-denominator primitives and project the resulting Fieller-type region onto multiple ratios without assuming denominators identify them.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Supershort calibration is a dependent system of ratios of asymptotically normal coefficient changes, matching the multiple-ratio discontinuity handled by primitive-space inversion.

open_problems.open_problem: Develop closure-complete log-cycle and Farkas feasibility certificates for sparse positive-ratio graphs and prove exact branch-LP or MILP computation across zero-bias strata, equality cycles, and optimizer ties.

source_refs.claim: The multi-setting construction applies pairwise ratio restrictions but computes projections only after replacing them with pairwise bias-difference bounds.
source_refs.author: Nick Huntington-Klein

source_refs.claim: Characterizes partially identified sets by finite inequalities and provides combinatorial and convex-optimization algorithms for exact compatibility checks.
source_refs.author: Alfred Galichon and Marc Henry

source_refs.claim: Develops a necessary-and-sufficient test for linear restrictions represented through a polyhedral cone and demonstrates computational feasibility.
source_refs.author: Yuichi Kitamura and Jorg Stoye

source_refs.excerpt: UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Implement the exchange-cycle partition and complete boundary-isolation certificate
exact agreement of all cells, boundary roots, intervals, singleton points, endpoints, labels, and rays
fixed-statistic root inversion cannot certify the topology without the exchange-cycle partition

open_problems.why_unsolved: This is a technique-derived transfer of finite compatibility and conic-duality machinery to Huntington-Klein's sparse ratio graph. On a strictly positive or negative branch, x_i = log|B_i| turns ratio bands into difference constraints, but this representation omits zero-bias faces where logs are undefined; local pairwise consistency also does not by itself certify one global bias assignment around every directed cycle. The first proof step that changes is a stratified equivalence between the primitive multiplicative constraints, all directed log-cycle inequalities, and a Farkas dual that remains correct on zero strata. The BudgetIV run shows why optimizing frozen branches without an exchange/tie certificate is insufficient, and targeted web searches found no existing OVB target-method pair.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A finite necessary-and-sufficient cycle-inequality system with explicit Farkas infeasibility witnesses and closure-correct zero-coordinate strata, plus a certified two-branch LP or binary MILP whose feasible set and optima agree with exhaustive primitive ratio feasibility in all equality and tie cases.

writing_exemplar.why: It introduces the sparse pairwise restriction graph and LP workflow whose missing global-compatibility layer motivates the certificate problem.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Researchers posit relationships only for credible setting pairs -> local positive-ratio bands must come from one global bias vector -> cycles, zero faces, and ties can make locally plausible restrictions incompatible -> exact certificates and branch-aware algorithms are needed

method_exemplars.technique: Replace an existential latent-model condition by a finite family of inequalities and use combinatorial or convex dual algorithms for exact membership.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The destination theorem must eliminate latent pairwise ratios without losing global compatibility and return a finite, checkable exact condition.

method_exemplars.technique: Use equivalent primal and dual polyhedral-cone representations to obtain a necessary-and-sufficient compatibility test.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Each connected fixed-sign OVB component is a finite cone-and-box feasibility problem, while a violated cycle should induce a short separating certificate.

method_exemplars.technique: Construct uniformly valid projected intervals by calibrated relaxation and repeated optimization-based feasibility checks.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Once exact, the branch solver can act as the inner feasibility oracle for inference on projected OVB endpoints.

open_problems.open_problem: For arbitrary requested pins on a subset of settings, characterize the exact sharp OVB endpoint gaps and decide when the pins are redundant, infeasible, or jointly binding under one common same-sign bias vector.

source_refs.claim: The paper explores its joint outer polytope through pinning, but it does not characterize sharp pin slices of the primitive positive-ratio model or their attainability.
source_refs.author: Nick Huntington-Klein

source_refs.excerpt: Extend the attainment construction to a jointly sharp vector of benefit, no-harm, and large-gain tier events
prove Delta=0 iff its endpoint law satisfies the common-alpha equations
if pi_sigma^PF is globally sharp ... then C_sigma(d;P) holds

open_problems.why_unsolved: Huntington-Klein's pinning operates on the bias-difference outer polytope, so it can report a nonempty or overly wide slice even when no bias vector in either sharp sign component satisfies all requested equalities. The prior catalogue repeatedly identifies the same joint-attainability obstruction: separately sharp coordinates or armwise rectangles need not be realized by one latent law. The first missing step is to construct one branch-specific omitted-variable completion satisfying all pins simultaneously and to use the branch-LP dual to distinguish redundant, infeasible, and binding pins; solving each pin separately manufactures a Cartesian product with no common witness.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A piecewise-linear sharp pinned-endpoint value function with necessary-and-sufficient primal-dual certificates for pin redundancy, infeasibility, and joint binding, a simultaneous-attainability theorem, and an explicit nondegenerate design where outer-polytope pinning understates the exact joint pin gap.

writing_exemplar.why: Its pinning workflow and ACS returns-to-college example directly frame why users need exact conditional slices rather than marginal outer-polytope answers.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Users pin plausible effects in selected settings -> the remaining effects should reflect the same latent bias vector -> separate or outer-polytope pin calculations can violate joint compatibility -> sharp pin slices need exact gap and feasibility certificates

method_exemplars.technique: Augment finite cone membership with equality restrictions and use primal-dual separation to certify feasibility or emptiness.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Requested pins are equality slices of each sharp bias component, and exact emptiness or binding status is a constrained compatibility question.

method_exemplars.technique: Optimize causal targets over a constrained latent feasible set and prove endpoint attainability by an explicit compatible distribution.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The pin gap must be an attained conditional identified-set endpoint under one common latent completion, not merely an LP value from relaxed coordinates.

method_exemplars.technique: Calibrate confidence limits for projections of parameters constrained by sample moment equalities and inequalities.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Pinned OVB endpoints are projections of equality-sliced sign branches and therefore admit an estimation and inference rung based on repeated feasibility optimization.

literature_map:
Huntington-Klein (2026, arXiv:2605.25483) introduces positive cross-setting OVB-ratio restrictions, a pairwise bias-difference polytope, LP projections, pinning, supershort calibration, and ACS returns-to-college illustrations.
Its Proposition 4 is a containment result for the difference polytope; no converse or sharpness claim was found, although Assumption 3 makes common sign substantive.
The paper explicitly labels sampling inference for the multi-setting joint polytope as future work and warns that supershort ratios are unstable near zero denominators.
PyPI records hetset 0.1.0 as an alpha Python release dated May 26, 2026; the manuscript also advertises R/CRAN and Stata/SSC implementations.
Cinelli and Hazlett (2020, JRSSB, 10.1111/rssb.12348) supply the partial-R2 OVB calculus and observed-covariate benchmarking used as the single-setting substrate.
Oster (2019, JBES, 10.1080/07350015.2016.1227711) anchors coefficient-stability sensitivity, while Diegert, Masten, and Poirier (arXiv:2206.02303) show benchmarking can fail with endogenous controls.
Chernozhukov, Cinelli, Newey, Sharma, and Syrgkanis (2026, REStat, arXiv:2112.13398) give sharp OVB bounds and efficient inference for broad causal functionals, but not cross-setting ratio closure.
Balke and Pearl (1997, JASA, 10.1080/01621459.1997.10474074) are the canonical LP-plus-attainability exemplar for proving causal bounds sharp rather than merely valid.
Galichon and Henry (2011, ReStud, 10.1093/restud/rdr008) and Kitamura and Stoye (2018, Econometrica, arXiv:1606.04819) provide finite-inequality, combinatorial, and conic-duality templates for exact compatibility certificates.
Imbens and Manski (2004, Econometrica, 10.1111/j.1468-0262.2004.00555.x) and Stoye (2009, Econometrica, 10.3982/ECTA7347) establish the single-interval inference benchmark that Huntington-Klein cites but does not extend.
Kaido, Molinari, and Stoye (2019, Econometrica, arXiv:1601.00934) supply uniformly valid calibrated projection and an optimization-based computational template.
Fang and Santos (2019, ReStud, arXiv:1404.3763) prove ordinary-bootstrap failure for non-fully differentiable maps; Hong and Li (2018, JoE, 10.1016/j.jeconom.2018.06.007) provide numerical-delta inference for directional maps.
Bolduc, Khalaf, and Yelou (2010, JoE), Dufour (1997, Econometrica), and Andrews and Mikusheva (2016, Econometrica) jointly show why near-zero ratio inference requires identification-robust inversion and may produce unbounded regions.
Targeted searches found no later work combining multi-setting OVB ratios with sharp sign-branch closure, log-cycle certificates, exact pinning, or singularity-robust supershort inference.
